subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Gamma-Ray Bursts
description: A short lesson to help you apply Gamma-Ray Bursts.

hook.text: Gamma-ray bursts are the most powerful explosions ever. In seconds, one releases more energy than the Sun will in its entire life.

buildup.text: They were discovered accidentally in 1967 by satellites monitoring nuclear tests. The bursts came from deep space.

discovery.text: Short bursts (under 2 seconds) come from neutron star mergers. Long bursts come from massive stars collapsing into black holes.

twist.text: A GRB aimed at Earth from a few thousand light-years away could cause a mass extinction by destroying the ozone layer.

climax.text: In 2022, the BOAT (Brightest Of All Time) GRB hit Earth's detectors so hard it briefly disrupted the ionosphere.

punchline.text: Seconds of energy exceeding the Sun's lifetime output. The universe's ultimate explosions.

quiz.question: How were gamma-ray bursts first discovered?
options: Accidentally by military satellites monitoring for nuclear weapons tests in 1967
By a dedicated gamma-ray telescope launched specifically to find them
Through mathematical predictions based on Einstein's relativity equations

details.summary: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are the most energetic explosions in the universe — brief flashes of gamma radiation that can release more energy in seconds than the Sun will in its entire lifetime. Long bursts come from collapsing massive stars; short bursts come from merging neutron stars.
details.whyItMatters: GRBs probe the most extreme physics in the universe. Short GRBs from neutron star mergers produce heavy elements like gold, connecting the most violent events to the origins of precious materials on Earth.
takeaways: The most energetic explosions in the known universe
Long bursts from massive star collapse, short from neutron star mergers
Release more energy in seconds than the Sun emits in its lifetime

faq.question: Could a gamma-ray burst threaten Earth?
faq.answer: If one occurred within a few thousand light-years and its beam were aimed at us, it could strip the ozone layer and cause a mass extinction. The probability is very low — no known progenitor star is close enough and aimed at Earth.

faq.question: How were gamma-ray bursts discovered?
faq.answer: Accidentally, during the Cold War. In the late 1960s, US Vela satellites designed to detect secret nuclear tests instead detected mysterious bursts of gamma rays from space. The discovery was declassified in 1973. Their cosmic origin wasn't confirmed until the late 1990s.
